messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Esperanto, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Esperanto line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
73 Poeto estis mi kaj kantis pri tiu justa 74 filo de Anchiso kiu venis de Trojo, 75 post la fiera Ilio estis bruligita.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑conditions) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | Poeta | speaker’s artistic identity (poet) | Poeto | poet | OK | | fui | copular past “was” + speaker identity | estis mi | was I | OK | | e | coordinator linking two clauses | kaj | and | OK | | cantai | past action “sang” about something | kantis | sang | OK | | di | preposition introducing object of singing | pri | about/of | OK | | quel | demonstrative determiner “that” | tiu | that | OK | | giusto | adjective describing the son as just | justa | just | OK | | figliuol | male child, son of Anchises | filo | son | OK | | d'Anchise | genitive indicating parent‑child relation | de Anchiso | of Anchises | OK | | che (relative) | introduces relative clause “who …” | kiu | who | OK | | venne | past motion “came” from Troy | venis | came | OK | | di (origin) | preposition marking source/origin | de | from | OK | | Troia | proper name “Troy” | Trojo | Troy | OK | | poi | temporal adverb “after” | post | after | OK | | che (subordinating) | resultative/conjunctive “that” (linking clause) – not needed in Esperanto | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | 'l | definite article “the” | la | the | OK | | superbo | adjective “proud” | fiera | proud | OK | | Ilïón | proper name “Ilion” (the city) | Ilio | Ilion | OK | | fu | auxiliary copula “was” (passive) | estis | was | OK | | combusto | past participle passive “burned” | bruligita | burned | OK |
### Items flagged - **UNNECESSARY**: the second *che* (line 75) – Esperanto does not require a conjunction here; the temporal adverb *post* already conveys the relationship.
No source words are missing, wrongly translated, or grammatically mismatched.
